questions.q: Why does this lesson use DAX measures instead of dragging the TotalSalesAmount and OrderCount columns directly onto the KPI cards?
options: Measures run faster than columns in every case
Measures recalculate correctly as filters (like a future region slicer) are applied, which a raw column only appears to do by coincidence on pre-aggregated data
DAX measures are required before any slicer can be added to a report
Power BI does not allow raw columns to be placed on card visuals
questions.explain: In a larger model with unaggregated rows, dragging a raw column onto a card wouldn't correctly respond to filters — writing measures is the habit that scales, even when a shortcut works today.

questions.q: Why does the Order Count measure use SUM(RegionalSalesSnapshot[OrderCount]) instead of DISTINCTCOUNT?
options: OrderCount is already a column of pre-counted numbers from the T-SQL query's COUNT(DISTINCT SalesOrderID), so summing those numbers across rows gives the correct total
DISTINCTCOUNT is not a valid DAX function
OrderCount contains text values that DISTINCTCOUNT cannot process
SUM always runs faster than DISTINCTCOUNT regardless of the data
questions.explain: Using DISTINCTCOUNT on an already-counted column would count how many distinct order-count values exist, not how many orders there were — a meaningless result.

questions.q: What does the Average Order Value measure, DIVIDE([Total Sales], [Order Count]), reference?
options: Only the raw TotalSalesAmount and OrderCount columns
The ProductLine and Territory columns
The Total Sales and Order Count measures, not the raw columns directly
A hardcoded average calculated once in Power Query
questions.explain: Building Average Order Value on top of the other two measures means it automatically inherits their correct filter behavior rather than duplicating logic.

questions.q: Why does Average Order Value use DIVIDE instead of a plain division operator (/)?
options: DAX does not support the / operator at all
DIVIDE returns blank instead of raising an error if Order Count is ever zero for a filtered combination
DIVIDE calculates faster than the / operator in every scenario
DIVIDE is required whenever two measures (rather than columns) are divided
questions.explain: Once a region slicer exists, some filtered combinations could have zero orders; DIVIDE handles that safely by returning blank rather than erroring.

questions.q: Where should these three DAX measures be created in the Power BI model?
options: Inside the T-SQL query's SELECT list, as additional computed columns
As Power Query calculated columns created during the Transform Data step
Directly inside each visual's formatting pane, one copy per visual
As measures in the Fields pane (or formula bar), not as calculated columns and not baked into the T-SQL query
questions.explain: Keeping them as measures lets Total Sales, Order Count, and Average Order Value be reused across the KPI cards, bar chart, and table without duplication.
